headline: Next national election will be held under caretaker government, says Home Minister
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced that political consensus has been reached, and a constitutional amendment is needed to formally restore the system, despite a Supreme Court decision.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced yesterday that the next national election will be held under a caretaker government. He stated this system would be restored through a constitutional amendment, confirming it at a press briefing.

Salahuddin Ahmed added that political consensus has already been reached on the issue. He referenced the Supreme Court's decision on the 13th amendment, which judicially revived the caretaker government system by overturning an earlier judgment.

The Minister emphasized that a constitutional amendment is still required to formally reinstate the system. He affirmed the government's commitment, noting that restoring the caretaker government was a key demand of their movement.

Regarding social media reports about ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina's potential return in December, Salahuddin said the government is aware. Bangladesh has sent multiple requests to India via the foreign ministry for her return under the extradition treaty.

On the situation in Sajek, Salahuddin reported that law and order have been brought under control. He mentioned various groups, including PCJSS and UPDF factions, were involved in disputes and control attempts during the tourism season.

The government and army have implemented measures to maintain peace in Sajek, with ongoing talks involving local leaders and headmen. These efforts aim to resolve internal conflicts and ensure stability in the region.

Addressing allegations against an additional DIG of police concerning a raid at his Purbachol house, Salahuddin confirmed the officer has been attached. Departmental proceedings will be initiated, following all legal procedures without considering identity.
caption:
Bangladesh's Home Minister confirms the next national election will be held under a caretaker government. A constitutional amendment is required to formally restore the system.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced yesterday that the next national election will be held under a caretaker government. He stated this system would be restored through a constitutional amendment, confirming it at a press briefing.

Salahuddin Ahmed added that political consensus has already been reached on the issue. He referenced the Supreme Court's decision on the 13th amendment, which judicially revived the caretaker government system by overturning an earlier judgment.

The Minister emphasized that a constitutional amendment is still required to formally reinstate the system. He affirmed the government's commitment, noting that restoring the caretaker government was a key demand of their movement.

Regarding social media reports about ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina's potential return in December, Salahuddin said the government is aware. Bangladesh has sent multiple requests to India via the foreign ministry for her return under the extradition treaty.

On the situation in Sajek, Salahuddin reported that law and order have been brought under control. He mentioned various groups, including PCJSS and UPDF factions, were involved in disputes and control attempts during the tourism season.

The government and army have implemented measures to maintain peace in Sajek, with ongoing talks involving local leaders and headmen. These efforts aim to resolve internal conflicts and ensure stability in the region.

Addressing allegations against an additional DIG of police concerning a raid at his Purbachol house, Salahuddin confirmed the officer has been attached. Departmental proceedings will be initiated, following all legal procedures without considering identity.

headline_marked: [[Gas, electricity disconnection]] among 5 penalties for not filing income tax return
headline: Gas, electricity disconnection among 5 penalties for not filing income tax return
summary: Tax officials can impose fines up to BDT 50,000 and cut utility connections for those who fail to submit their income tax returns on time. This affects millions of TIN holders in Bangladesh.
details: Failure to submit income tax returns on time can lead to severe penalties, including fines up to BDT 50,000 and the disconnection of essential utility services like gas and electricity.
Bangladesh currently has 1.25 crore Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) holders, but only about 50 lakh taxpayers submit their returns annually, leaving a significant number of non-filers.
While not all TIN holders are legally required to file, it is mandatory for those with taxable income or for accessing 45 types of government and private services.

The Income Tax Act outlines five types of consequences for non-compliance. Under Section 266, tax officials can impose a penalty of 10% of the last assessed tax, with a minimum of BDT 1,000 and a maximum of BDT 50,000.
Additionally, a daily fine of BDT 50 can be levied for continued failure, and a BDT 50,000 fine may be imposed if requested information is not provided during an investigation.

Failure to file returns on time also results in the loss of tax exemption benefits, as per Section 174 of the Income Tax Act. Taxpayers will not receive tax breaks on investments in government-specified sectors, such as savings certificates.
An extra 2% tax per month will be charged on the imposed tax for returns filed past the deadline. This adds to the financial burden on non-compliant individuals.
Tax officials are empowered to disconnect gas, electricity, and even water connections for both residential and industrial users who do not submit their income tax returns.

For high-grade government and private sector officials, filing returns is mandatory. Non-submission can lead to complications in receiving salaries and allowances, as offices often require proof of return submission.

From the current fiscal year, returns can be filed year-round. Tax exemptions are available for returns filed between July and September, while regular tax applies from October to December. Returns filed from January to June will incur penalties along with the tax.
